customer: Okay so I'm on my break at the hospital (night shift, so my brain is a little fried, sorry) and I've been thinking about getting out of the lease on my pickup because honestly I barely drive it anywhere except to and from work. Someone told me I could just sell it to you, but it's leased, so I don't even know if that's a thing? I'm in Eastvale if that matters, and I really don't have a lot of free daytime hours to chase paperwork, so I'm hoping it isn't a huge ordeal.
agent: Yes, you can sell us a leased truck. Because the leasing company owns it, the sale works as a buyout from them, so first check that your leasing company allows third-party buyouts (see our article "Which leasing companies allow third-party buyouts"). To keep the paperwork light, you can sign the lease buyout authorization, form NW-LSE-1, and we'll request the dealer payoff quote for you, which can be different from the payoff they quote to you. Then bring that quote to your appointment, and if our offer comes in higher than the buyout, see "If our offer is more than your lease buyout" for what happens next.
